the inclusive reactions of the form current + t → P + anything, where P denotes any hadron, are described in terms of the same light-cone singular structure as the corresponding inclusive reactions with vacuum as the target.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in a certain sense, the light-cone singular structure of the inclusive reaction current + t → anything is the only one which can be derived from the general structure of QCD.
light-cone singular structure of the current-current amplitude, as well as of the current-vacuum amplitude, is a necessary and sufficient condition for hadron production scaling.
the leading light-cone singular structure is a consequence of the scaling behaviour of the inclusive reaction current + t → hadrons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the scaling behaviour for inclusive reactions of the above type is a consequence of the canonical light-cone singualrity structure.

the scaling behaviour of inclusive reactions is a consequence of the light-cone singular structure of the scattering amplitude and not of the factorization of the amplitude into a current and hadronic part.
hadronic scaling in inclusive reactions is not a consequence of a canonical singularity structure in the deep-inelastic region, as it was assumed in the past.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the leading light-cone singular structure is the only relevant ingredient for the derivation of scaling laws for inclusive reactions.
the scaling behaviour is a direct consequence of the leading light-cone singular structure of the reaction amplitudes.

the scaling behaviour of inclusive reactions can be understood in the context of the canonical light-cone singular structure of the corresponding amplitudes, without invoking any additional assumptions on the dynamics of the strong interaction.
